body:
You are a dialogue and narration writer for a single-player dark-fantasy RPG based on Curse of Strahd, set in the gloomy, mist-bound valley of Barovia. Reply with plain text only (no JSON, no markdown, no code fences, no preamble, no commentary after) and do not send messages to any other agent. Write only what is asked, in the exact format asked.

SETTING OF THIS TASK: the catacombs under Castle Ravenloft, where the old house of von Zarovich buries its dead in rows of iron-gated crypts, each with a name over the gate. The party is level 10. Count Strahd von Zarovich is the vampire lord of the castle. The crypts are orderly, cold and almost tender; the horror is how long everything has waited. A few of the book's crypts are comic (a chef with a bell, a knight who tripped on his own sword, a rich man's painted gold coins). Those keep their joke deadpan and never wink at the player.

TONE: gothic horror with dry, understated, character-driven humour. Funny comes from specifics and deadpan, not from jokes about the horror. Where a scene is sad, let it be sad. No modern slang, no pop culture, no real-world references. Do not invent other named people than the ones given. Do not use em-dashes (use commas, colons or full stops). Do not use semicolons more than once in a line. Plain words a voice actor can read aloud.

NARRATOR STYLE (second person, present tense, one or two sentences). Samples from the existing game, to match voice, length and rhythm:
- A bronze plaque, green with age: the old king's champion, who never lost a fight. It lists the men he killed. It takes up the whole plaque.
- Over the foot of the stair, two words cut deep and plain: HE RESTS. Nothing about peace.
- The lord of the house in marble, seated, a wolf at his feet. The sculptor made him kinder than he is, and the stone has not forgiven either of them.
- Words are cut over the stair: the house keeps its dead. Someone has added, below it, in a smaller hand: and its dead keep the house.
Carved words are written in CAPITALS inside the sentence, as in the samples.

TASK: write ONE Narrator line for each slot below, in the format
SLOT_ID: the line
(one line per slot, nothing else). Each line is at most 32 words unless the slot says otherwise. Slots marked "epitaph" describe the words carved over a crypt gate or lintel: quote the carved words in CAPITALS, then add at most one short Narrator sentence. Never repeat a joke or a sentence shape between slots.

THE LESSER VAULTS: a second, older range of crypts reached by a stair down from the lower gallery, where the house buried the people it did not honour: servants, guildsmen, hangers-on, saints nobody visited, and a few that frightened the family.

VAULTS_ENTER: the party arrives in the Lesser Vaults at the foot of the stair. Narrow, low, older than the rest. At most 40 words.
MARKOVIA_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of Saint Markovia, a holy healer whom a valley abbey was named for.
MARKOVIA_DARTS: a trap fires in front of her sarcophagus: poisoned darts fly out of the walls. One or two sentences.
MARKOVIA_BONE: examine her sarcophagus: on the lid, wrapped in faded cloth, lies a long bone, her thighbone, kept as a holy relic. Hint that touching it is a sacred matter.
KHAZAN_DOOR: examine a shut crypt door that bears the name KHAZAN. Behind it there is nothing; the one who was buried there left long ago for a tower of his own. One or two sentences.
STAHBAL_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of Stahbal Indi-Bhak, a warlord from far away buried with his fifteen captains.
STAHBAL_SHAFT: examine the crypt: a round shaft opens in the floor and goes down into darkness, and around the walls stand coffins, many of them, every lid closed. Dread, no jokes.
STAHBAL_WIGHTS: the fight begins: lids lift and bones begin to rise from the walls. At most 38 words.
SASHA_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of Sasha Ivliskova, wife. Sad, tender, a little wrong.
PATRINA_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of Patrina Velikovna, a bride. (She is a ghost elsewhere now, but this stays the stone's text.)
PATRINA_BIER: examine the bier in her crypt: it is empty, the dust on it undisturbed, a few old coins in the corners. Hint that the dead woman is not here.
STEFAN_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of Stefan Gregorovich, counsellor to King Barov. A skull on a shelf inside can still speak.
INTREE_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of Intree Sik-Valoo, a scholar from far away. A skull on a shelf inside can still speak.
SPIDERS_ENTER: the party enters a nameless crypt choked with grey webs from floor to ceiling; the fight begins as heavy shapes drop out of the dark. At most 38 words.
FINDERWAY_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of Saint Finderway, patron of lost travellers: the carved words are PASS NOT THESE PORTALS, and nothing else.
FINDERWAY_ALCOVES: examine two stone alcoves facing each other in the crypt; the air in one hums faintly and the dust inside is disturbed, as if used. At most 34 words.
FINDERWAY_GO: the party steps into the humming alcove: the stone tilts, and an instant later they stand in another alcove, in a tomb. At most 28 words.
JARNWALD_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of Sir Jarnwald the Trickster. The joke is that the epitaph itself is a trick.
JARNWALD_FLOOR: a trap fires: the floor, which looked solid, was only an illusion, and everyone steps through it into a pit. At most 34 words.
JARNWALD_GHOULS: the fight begins: in the pit below, the ghouls that lived there lift their heads. At most 34 words.
result:
VAULTS_ENTER: The ceiling drops and the stone turns older, rougher, cut before the masons learned pride. Here the house laid those it needed, feared, or simply did not know where else to put.
MARKOVIA_EPITAPH: Above the gate: SAINT MARKOVIA, WHO MENDED WHAT WAS TORN. The iron latch has been oiled more recently than the rest, though not by anyone who prayed.
MARKOVIA_DARTS: A flagstone gives by a hair's breadth, and narrow iron needles hiss from the mortar on either side. Even the saint's floor was built by the lord of the castle.
MARKOVIA_BONE: On the stone lid rests a single long thighbone in faded linen, yellow as old tallow. Whatever mercy was left in her has settled into the marrow; take it only with clean hands.
KHAZAN_DOOR: Only one word is cut into the slab: KHAZAN. Behind the seam the air smells of nothing at all, as though the room were emptied when its tenant took a tower of his own.
STAHBAL_EPITAPH: The lintel reads: STAHBAL INDI-BHAK, A GREAT GENERAL FROM A DISTANT LAND. He brought fifteen captains into the valley, and the valley kept the set.
STAHBAL_SHAFT: In the middle of the floor a round well drops straight down out of sight. Upright coffins line the walls like guards at attention, fifteen shut lids waiting for an order.
STAHBAL_WIGHTS: Wood groans against dry wood as fifteen lids shift at once. Gaunt hands take the rims from within, and old Campaign iron scrapes the stone as the general's men form ranks.
SASHA_EPITAPH: Cut cleanly over the bars: SASHA IVLISKOVA, WIFE. No dates are given, as if the marriage only began when the gate was locked.
PATRINA_EPITAPH: The stone over the arch reads: PATRINA VELIKOVNA, BRIDE. The carver left room for a second name, and never came back with the chisel.
PATRINA_BIER: The stone bed is bare, its grey dust smooth from edge to edge save for a few tarnished coins in the corners. Whoever was promised this room found somewhere else to walk.
STEFAN_EPITAPH: The inscription reads: STEFAN GREGOROVICH, COUNSELLOR TO KING BAROV, WHOSE WORD ENDED ARGUMENTS. Inside, on a narrow shelf, a clean skull faces the grate as if waiting to be asked.
INTREE_EPITAPH: Carved in careful letters: INTREE SIK-VALOO, SCHOLAR OF STRANGE TONGUES. The house took his body for the vault and left his head on the shelf, where it could still be useful.
SPIDERS_ENTER: The name over the arch is gone under a curtain of thick grey web that sways as the gate opens. High in the dark, heavy bodies unhook their legs from the ceiling and drop.
FINDERWAY_EPITAPH: Over the gate of Saint Finderway, patron of lost travellers, the stone says only: PASS NOT THESE PORTALS. For a guide of the lost, his advice is very short.
FINDERWAY_ALCOVES: Two stone niches face each other across the narrow floor. One is thick with undisturbed dust; in the other the air hums against your teeth, and bootmarks end at the wall.
FINDERWAY_GO: You step into the humming niche and the stone tilts under your heel. Between one breath and the next, the crypt is gone and another tomb closes round you.
JARNWALD_EPITAPH: High on the lintel, in tiny letters that draw you two steps past the threshold to read them: SIR JARNWALD THE TRICKSTER, LOOK DOWN.
JARNWALD_FLOOR: Your boot goes straight through the painted grey flagstones as though they were smoke. The real floor is a dark pit ten feet lower.
JARNWALD_GHOULS: Down in the mire at the bottom of the shaft, pale shapes stop gnawing on the last guest and turn their wet faces toward the light.
